questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had several aspects being crucial to my choosing of IReland af my destination but a further development of language skills and the habitants of the country were the most important.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The irish people are among the friendliest i have ever met and they have a rich academic heritage.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international office of UCC (University College Cork) were very competent in giving information and having orientations before the semester started. The only thing is if you travel as a law student you should be informed that the course selection process is different and you should contact the UCC international office regarding this.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a whole day of orientation where the international office  went through every aspect of studying abroad. Very informative.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Only thing i missed was more detailed information regarding course selection as a law student as this process was diffferent,

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I filled in a survey sent to me by the host uni and they found accommodation for me. This is necessary as the housing situation in Ireland is very difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are many good places to live off campus in student accommodations but it is not cheap. I will recommend not asking for the cheapest one though as you really get what you pay for.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a place called Edenhall and it was one of the cheapest options but it was not a nice place to live to say the least.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As a law student i had a different course selection process as my fellow exchange students. I had to find the relevant cources and send in a document directly to the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people at the international office were at my service and helped me with every question i had.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all of the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware if you are a law student and let the people at UCC know right away as the registration process is different.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one BA course and three MA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is similar but be prepared that the exam style is different as it is essay writings and hand written exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Law of Contract, Contemporary Issues in Corporate law, Economic Law of the European Union and Law of Cybercrime.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them but especially Law of Contracts or Contemporary Issues in Corporate Law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing I was not prepared for

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the football club and the the student union was really good at hosting different events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different student societies so my recommendation is to find one that interests you and join. Also, join the events planned by the student union.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go rent a car and drive around Ireland. Its the most beautiful country in Europe.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as the irish people are very nice and friendly. The only this is they can be difficult to understand at times.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Every thing is more old fashioned in regard to digital tools and infrastructure.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture of going out and meet each other over a drink.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for the language, be open minded and seek the local people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare your essays in good time as they are usually due at the same time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people to build an international network and being introduced to a new country's academic culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settleing to a new way of doing exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
